newsitem.title: SPAIN: NATO sees Russian arms threat rise-Spanish report.
newsitem.headline: NATO sees Russian arms threat rise-Spanish report.

text.p: A secret NATO report sees Russian arms posing a growing military threat to the alliance because of corruption, unchecked exports and a surplus of weapons designers with deadly skills, a Spanish newspaper said on Monday.
"The potential threat to NATO stemming from Russian arms proliferation could increase," the daily El Mundo quoted the document as saying.

It listed, "a combination of factors such as weak exports control, hundreds of scientists specialised in building chemical, bacteriological and nuclear agents, the high degree of corruption or the deliberate exchange of nuclear technology."

The report, numbered MC 161/96 and titled "The general intelligence estimate - strategic overview", was put together by NATO intelligence experts at Brussels headquarters and has been circulated to the 16 member states, the daily added.
El Mundo said it had obtained a copy of the paper, which is labelled "NATO Secret".
Parliament voted this month to have Spain join the alliance's military structure, a move which the daily says could make Spanish territory a more immediate target for attacks.

The leaked document was published just one week before a European security summit that starts in Lisbon next Monday. It could prove an embarrassment to Western nations as they try to use the meeting to allay Russian concerns over NATO enlargement.
El Mundo said the report singles out Russia, Libya, Syria, Iran and Iraq as potential foes of the U.S.-led alliance but sees north Africa as the top source of threats to its territory.
It says Libya could pose a significant threat in 10 years' time if Tripoli successfully develops long-range missiles and warheads which could put Spain within its range.
"As long as (Libyan leader Muammar) Gaddafi remains in power, there is a potential threat of the use in the future of weapons of mass destruction," El Mundo quoted the paper as saying.
